name: Obadiah

objectives.text: Identify Obadiah as the shortest book in the Old Testament and as a prophet who received a message from God
Retell that Jacob and Esau were twin brothers whose families grew into the nations of Israel and Edom
Describe what Edom did wrong when Jerusalem was attacked and explain from Scripture why God's people should not be glad when others are hurt
Identify God's promise in Obadiah to rescue His people on Mount Zion and to rule as King
Summarize the conflict between Jacob and Esau in Genesis, including the birthright, the stolen blessing, and their later meeting
Explain how Edom's pride in its high rocky home deceived it and how Scripture teaches that God brings the proud low
Locate Edom on a map of the ancient Near East and describe how its mountainous terrain made it feel secure
Outline the structure of Obadiah as judgment on Edom, the day of the Lord on the nations, and the restoration of Zion
Explain why Obadiah treats Edom's violence as a sin against a brother using God's earlier instruction about Edom
Analyze the historical setting of Obadiah and weigh the evidence for linking it to the Babylonian fall of Jerusalem
Interpret the announcement that the day of the Lord is near upon all the nations, including the image of drinking the cup of judgment
Connect the judgment of Edom to the deliverance and holiness promised for Mount Zion and the house of Jacob
Construct a timeline of relations between Israel and Edom from the patriarchs through the exile using biblical texts
Explain the principle that as you have done it shall be done to you and compare it with other biblical statements of reciprocal justice
Distinguish God's just judgment of Edom from personal revenge using the New Testament teaching on vengeance and love of enemies
Compare Obadiah's oracle with the parallel oracle against Edom in Jeremiah and identify shared wording and distinct emphases
Analyze the escalating sins of Edom in Obadiah from standing aloof to gloating, looting, and handing over survivors as failures to love one's neighbor
Defend the Reformed teaching that God justly governs and judges the nations using Obadiah and related texts
Explain how the promise that the kingdom shall be the Lord's is developed through the prophets and fulfilled in Christ's reign, including the gathering of the nations

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (short book, Jacob and Esau, gloating, pride and the rocky fortress, historical background, day of the Lord, Zion, reciprocal justice, history of conflict, God's justice, the kingdom). Merged the pride warning into the pride objective and changed the vague observation about God defending His people into a text-based identification of the Zion promise. Turned the grade 11 gloating evaluation into an analysis of the escalating sins in verses 11-14 so it does not repeat the grade 2 objective. Added map and terrain, book structure, the brotherhood obligation, the parallel with Jeremiah 49, and the distinction between divine judgment and personal revenge. Anchored the objectives in specific verses and attached confession references only where they state the doctrine taught.
